definition: <theih>, be able, and <tawp>, the limit: placed after a verb or describing word and followed by <in> or <un>, it says that the thing is done to the furthest degree possible; {a hat theih tawp un} is as fast as they could

terms: as much as possible/to the best of one's ability/as far as one can
definition: <theih>, be able, and <tawpin>, to the utmost: placed after a verb, to the limit of what can be done; {ka hih theih tawpin} is as much as I can do, and {hanciam theih tawpin} trying as hard as possible
<theih>, know, and <ban>, reach, written as one word; {theihban zawhloh} is what knowledge cannot reach, unknown or beyond understanding
<theih>, <ban> and <loh> written as one word: what one's knowing does not reach, be beyond one's knowledge
<theih>, know, with <bat>, reach, written as one word: as far as knowledge reaches; {ka theihbat tanh} is as far as I know, and {theihbat loh} is what is beyond one's knowledge
<theih>, know, with the ending {-beh}, more, in addition: come to know more; {theihbeh nop a om leh} is if anyone wishes to know more
<theihbeh>, know more, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that is worth knowing in addition; {theihbehhuai aomte} is further things worth knowing
<theihnop>, want to know, and {theih beh}, know further, written as one word: wish to know more about a matter
<theih>, know, and <cian>, clearly, written as one word: know a thing exactly and for certain; {ki theihcian} is be found out for certain
<theihcian> and <ding> written as one word: what is to be known clearly, or in order that someone knows it for certain
<theih> and <ciang> written as one word: as far as is known, what one knows, or when it became known
<theih> and <ciangin> written as one word: when someone comes to know something, or after another verb when it could be done
noun of <theihcian>: knowing a thing clearly and for certain; {theihcianna om lo} is nothing is known for certain
<theih>, know, with <ciat>, each, written as one word: known to each one; {i theihciat} is what we all know
<theih> and <cil> written as one word: the first knowing of a thing, when it is first noticed; {ka theihcil akipan} is since I first knew, as long as I remember
<theih>, know, and <dan>, way, written as one word: the way someone knows or understands a thing, what one knows of it; {ka theihdan} is as far as I know
<theih> and <ding> written as one word: what is to be known, things one should know; after another verb, so as to be able to

terms: for the information of/so as to know
definition: <theih>, know, and <dingin>, in order to, written as one word: so that someone may know, placed after those who are to know
<theih>, know, with <hak>, hard: difficult to know or understand, said of a saying or riddle
<theih>, know, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that ought to be known; {a theihhuai} is the things worth knowing
<theihhuai>, worth knowing, with <sa>, consider: find that something ought to be known and therefore tell it
<thei>, able, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word after a verb: closes a statement that something can be done or may happen
<thei>, can, and the question particle <hiam> written as one word: could it, how could it; closes an indirect question, as in {banghangin puakkham theihiam}, why it could explode

terms: before/in the presence of/with the knowledge of
definition: <theih>, know, with the ending <in>, placed after a possessive: with that person knowing, in the hearing or sight of; {mite’ theihin} is before people, openly
<theih>, be able, and the negative <kei> written as one word, after a verb and mostly before <leh>, if: {theihkei leh} is if one cannot
<theih>, know, with <khak>, happen to: come to know or learn something
<theih>, know, and <khialh.2>, wrongly, written as one word: understand wrongly; {ka theihkhialh kei leh} is if I am not mistaken
<theih>, know, with <khiat>, out: come to know by searching; the form used before a noun or <zawh>
<theihkhiat>, find out, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of finding out or coming to know something

terms: have come to know/know fully/finish learning
definition: <theih>, know, with <khit>, finished: {theihkhit ciangin} is after one has come to know, {theihkhit phetin} as soon as one knows

terms: have been able to/have managed to
definition: after another verb, <theih>, form of <thei>, can, with <khit>, finished: the action has been achieved, as in {aphelh theihkhit uhciangin}, after they were able to put it out; not the verb know of the other sense
<theihkhit> have come to know, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of already knowing
<theih>, know, with <khol>, beforehand: know in advance
<theih>, know, with <kholh>, beforehand; {theihkholh lohin}, without knowing beforehand, means unexpectedly, suddenly
<theihkholh> know beforehand with the noun suffix <na>
<theih> able with <kik> again and the noun suffix <na>; {khua muh theihkikna} is the regaining of sight
<theih>, know, with <kim>, all: known to everyone, well known or in common use
<theih>, know, with <kim>, all: of everyone, come to know; also be known by all
<theih> know or able with <lam> way, manner; in the verse, that someone is able to know all mysteries

terms: come to know/get to know/learn of
definition: <theih>, know, with <lawh>, here gain as a result: come to know something through an event or through someone; {ki theihlawh} is get acquainted with one another
<theih> and <leh> written as one word: if one can; {ahih theihleh} is if possible
<theih> know and <lo> not written as one word: not knowing, not known, without someone knowing
<theih> and <loh> written as one word, the form of {thei lo} used before a noun or <ding>: after a verb, that cannot be done; alone, not knowing or what is not known
<theihloh>, not knowing, and <kalin>, while: while one does not know or notice, unawares; stands at the head of a clause or after a subject marker, as in {i theihloh kalin}, without our noticing

terms: so that it is not possible/to prevent from/lest
definition: <theihloh>, cannot, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the action cannot be done, to keep someone from doing it; the clause it closes gives the purpose of the main verb that follows; the negative of <theih nadingin>

terms: so as not to know/so as not to be able
definition: <theihloh> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: so that it is not known or cannot be done, as in {amuh theihlohding in}, so that he or she could not see
<theih>, know, <loh>, not, and <kal>, interval, written as one word: while someone does not know or notice; after a possessive and before <in>, as in {na theihlohkal in}, without your noticing

terms: because of not knowing/out of ignorance
definition: <theih> and <lohman> written as one word: because one does not know, or what comes only from not knowing
<theih>, know, with <loh>, not, and the noun suffix <na>: not knowing, ignorance; {theihlohna hangin} is through ignorance, unintentionally
after a verb, where <theih> means can and not know: not being able to do what that verb says, as <ihmut theihlohna>, being unable to sleep, and {lungkim theihlohna}, being unable to be content
plural of <theihlohna>; after a verb it names the things one is not able to do, as {na hih theihlohnate}, the things you cannot do
<theih>, know or be able, and <luat>, so very, written as one word: know something only too well; in some sentences be very possible
<theih> able with <ma> before, placed after a verb: before one could do it
<theih> in the sense know, with <ma> before: before one knew or came to know a thing, after a pronoun such as <a> or <i> and not after another verb; followed by <in> or {pek-pan}
<theih>, know, with the noun suffix <na>: what one knows, knowledge
the power to think and understand; {thu ngaihsut theihna} is good sense or discretion
<thei>, can, with the noun ending, after another verb: being able to do it; {theihna ding} or <theihna dingin> is so that it can be done, and {theihna lampi} is a way to do it

terms: so that it may be possible/in order to be able to
definition: <theihna>, here being able, and <dingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that it can be done; another way of writing <theih nadingin>

terms: so that they can/in order that they may
definition: <theihna>, here not knowledge but <thei>, be able, with <na>, and <dingun>, for them to: placed after a verb with <a> before it, so that they may be able to do it

terms: so as to be able to/in order to know
definition: <theih> and <nading> written as one word: after a verb, so that it can be done, in order to be able to; after a noun, in order to know it

terms: so that it can/in order to be able to
definition: <theihnading> and <in> written as one word after a verb: so that the action can be done

terms: so that one can/in order to be able
definition: <theih>, be able, with <nang>, a short form of <nading>, written as one word after a verb: so that it can be done, in order to be able to
plural of <theihna>, the things one knows; also the way one came to know something

after a verb, <theih> in its meaning can: the things one is able to do, or the possibility of doing them, as {hih theihnate}, what one can do, and {sepkhop theihnate}, being able to work together; not what one knows
<theih> know with <ngei> ever; with {nai lo}, have never yet known
<theihngei>, have ever known, with <loh>, not, written as one word before a noun: that one has never known
<theih> know, with <nop> want; the form used before a noun, as in {theihnop thu}, a thing someone wants to know
<theihnop>, want to know, and <leh>, if, written as one word; mostly {na theihnopleh}, if you want to know

terms: not want to know/unwillingness to know
definition: <theihnop> and <loh> written as one word: not wanting to know, set against <theihloh>, not knowing
<theihnop> want to know with the noun suffix <na>
<theihnop> want to know with the plural <te>; {thu theihnopte} are the matters people want to learn by inquiring
<theih> able with <pah> at once, placed after a verb: can do it right away
<theih> in its meaning know, not able, with <pah> at once: understand a thing immediately; the thing known stands before it, often ending in <lam>, and no other verb comes directly before {theihpah}

terms: know right away/be able right away
definition: <theih>, know or be able, and <pak>, quickly, written as one word: know offhand, or be able to do at once
<theih>, be able or know, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the fact of being able to do something, or what one knows, taken as the topic

terms: as soon as known/the moment it is known
definition: <theih>, know, and <phet>, as soon as, written as one word: {aki theihphet in} is as soon as it became known
know about a matter together with someone, so as to be a witness to it; {a theihpih mite} are the witnesses, and {theihpih lohin} is without the knowledge of
in the phrase {kisak theihpih}: be proud of something, boast in it
of a government or other authority: accept a body or a person as lawful and registered; {kumpi theihpih} before a noun is recognized by the government
<theihpih> and <lo>, not, written as one word: not know a matter along with someone, not understand what a person feels or does
<theihpih>, know of or recognize, with <loh>, not, written as one word: not known of or not recognized by the one named before it, as in {kumpi theihpihloh}, not recognized by the government
<theihpih> with the noun suffix {-na}: official recognition or acknowledgement, as given by a government
<theih>, know, with <sa>, which marks something already done: what one already knows or has come to know
in grammar, of a word that is not spoken or written because the hearer knows it already, as {kei in} in spoken style
in grammar, a subject that is not said because it is taken as known, as <Nang>, you, in the command {Hong tum ve}, come in; also called <nusiat a sempa>

terms: as we all know/known to everyone
definition: <theihsa>, already known, and <ciat>, each one: a thing that every one of us already knows; it follows <i> or <ih>, we, and closes a statement with {ahi hi}, or opens one as {ih theihsa ciat mah bang in}, just as we all know

terms: as we all know/known to everyone
definition: <theihsa>, already known, and <tek>, each one: what each of us already knows; stands after <i> or <ih>, we, and mostly before {mah bangin} or <mahbangin>, just as, to open a statement with a fact the reader knows
<theih>, know, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to know, make known, reveal or warn
<theihsak>, make known, and <ding> written as one word: to inform, that someone is to be told, often before <kisam>, it is necessary
<theihsak>, make known, with <na>: something that gives notice, such as a trumpet blast or a smoke signal; {theihsakna lim} is a sign

terms: want to make known/choose to reveal
definition: <theihsak>, make known, with <nop>, want: wish to make something known to someone; the form used before a noun

terms: wish to inform/intention to make known
definition: <theihsaknop>, want to make known, with the noun suffix <na>: the purpose of letting people know
<theih>, know, with <sasa>, already, written as one word: what or who was already known before

terms: try to know/seek to understand/find out
definition: <theih> and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: make an effort to know or learn about something
<theih>, know, with <siam>, skilled: grasp a matter rightly, or understand a person's situation with sympathy
<theih>, know, with <siam>, skilled, and the noun suffix <na>: the skill of knowing well, good judgment
<theih>, the form of <thei>, know, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: make known; the page lists the form without a meaning

terms: as far as one knows/what one knows
definition: <theih>, know, with the ending {-sun}, the full extent, after <ka>, <na> or a pronoun: all that one knows, as far as one knows; {ka theihsun tawm} is the little that I know

terms: know by oneself/find out on one's own
definition: <theih>, know, with <tawm>, by oneself: come to know something by one’s own effort, without being told
<theihtawm> know by oneself, with the noun suffix <na>
<theih> with plural <te> after a verb: the things that can be so used; {tum theihte} instruments that are played, {nek theihte} things that can be eaten
in {mel theihte}, those known by face
<theih>, know, with plural <te>, after <a> or <ka> and not after another verb: the things or the people that someone knows or has learned, where {nek theihte} is of what can be done
<theih>, know, and <tek>, each, written as one word: each one knows, every one of us knows
<theih>, know, with <tel>, clearly: know thoroughly; also used as a noun, full knowledge
<theihtel> understand with <hak> hard
clear and full knowing of a matter
plural of <theihtelna>
<theihtel> understand with <nop> want
<theih> know with <teng> all, the whole of
<theih>, know, and <thamloh> written as one word, followed by <in>: without the other person noticing it
in the verse the horns that scattered Judah; probably a misprint of <thehthang> scatter
<theih>, know, with <theih>, be able
after a descriptive word: as much as possible; {hunsau theihtheih} is as long a time as possible
<theih>, know, said twice: know as a matter of common knowledge, not be able to know; {i theihtheih sa} is what we all know already

terms: so that it may somehow be possible/in order to be able to know
definition: <theihtheih>, <theih> said twice, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the action may by any means become possible, said of repeated effort or coaxing toward that end; after an object without another verb, in order to be able to know it
the ability to know
after a descriptive word, a way of being so as far as possible; {hun sau theihtheihna}, a means of making the time as long as can be

terms: so that it may be possible/so as to be able
definition: <theihtheihna>, here being able as far as can be, and <dingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the act may be possible by whatever means, as {ngah theihtheihna dingin}, so as to be able to get
<theihtheih> with <sa> already done: what one has come to know

terms: worth knowing/that ought to be known
definition: <theih>, know, and <tuak>, be fitting, written as one word: that people should know or have a right to know
<thei>, know, with <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that ought to be known
<theih> able with <zah> amount, placed after a verb: to the extent one is able
be able to know or grasp; after a possessive, what someone is able to understand

terms: have known each other for/be acquainted since
definition: after <ki> and before a length of time: the time since two people came to know each other, as {kaki theihzawh uh kum 20}, we have known each other for 20 years; here <zawh> means since and not be able

terms: ability to know fully/ability to fathom
definition: <theihzawh> be able to know, with the noun suffix <na>
<theih> know with <zawk> more, used with <sangin> than
<theih> able with <zel> habitually, placed after a verb: something one tends to do again and again

terms: way of being able/how one can
definition: <theih>, be able, and <zia>, way, written as one word after a verb: the way in which something can be done
<thei>, know, and the linking <in>, written as one word: knowing it, and so doing what follows
<thei>, be able, and the linking <in>, written as one word after a verb: the action could be done, and what follows resulted
<thei>, able, and <kei>, not, written as one word and placed after a verb: cannot, is not able to
<thei> with the ending {-keng}, the negative of the first person singular, written as one word: I do not know; after a verb, I cannot
get to know or taste something for oneself; with {ngei lo} or {nai lo}, never having experienced
<theikha> and <lo> written as one word: not come to know of something, be unaware of it
<thei> know with <khawm> together
<thei>, know, with <khia>, out: come to know something by searching or thinking it through
<thei>, know, and <khial>, wrongly, written as one word: understand or take something wrongly; {ki theikhial} is be mistaken for or wrongly held to be so
<theikhia> with <pan>, here only then, written as one word: came to know at that point, found out for the first time
<thei> know, with <khin>, already, completely

terms: have been able to/have managed to
definition: after another verb, <thei>, be able, with <khin>, already: the action has already been achieved, as in {kikankhia theikhin}, has already been found out; here <thei> is not know
<thei>, know, with <khol>, ahead of time

terms: not know beforehand/not know in advance
definition: <theikhol>, know beforehand, and <lo>, not, written as one word, often after <bangmah>, nothing
<theikhol> know beforehand with the causative <sak>
<thei>, be able, with <kik>, again; {khua mu theikik} is be able to see again, regain sight
<thei> know with <kim> all: said of everyone knowing a thing, or of knowing the whole of it
<thei>, fig, with <kung>, tree: the fig tree
<theikung>, fig tree, capitalised in the text
<theikung> fig tree with <teng> all
<thei> able with <lai> still, placed after a verb: still able to do it
<thei.1>, know, with <lai>, still, after a subject marker such as <na>: still know or remember something; not the {theilai} that follows another verb and means still able

terms: will still be able to/may still
definition: <thei>, able, and <laiding> written as one word after a verb: will still be able to, may yet
<thei>, able, and <le>, if, written as one word after a verb: if one can do it; before <uhcin> it is a polite wish, if you could

terms: if you can/if you are able to
definition: <thei>, able, and <lecin>, if you, written as one word after a verb
<thei> and <leh> written as one word after a verb: if it can be done; {hi theileh} is if possible
<thei>, can, with <lel>, merely, written as one word after a verb: can do it just like that, with nothing more needed
<thei>, know or be able, and <leng>, if, written as one word: after a verb, if we could do it; alone, if we know; often followed by a statement that this would be good
after a verb, cannot; {pau theilo}, unable to speak, mute
<thei>, know, with <lo>, not: not know or not realise something
<theilo>, unable, and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will not be able to, is not to; with <in>, so that one cannot
form of <theilo> cannot, placed after a verb and before a noun: that cannot be done
<thei>, know, with the negative <loh>, placed before a noun: that one does not know, as {theiloh mite}, people one does not know; the other sense follows a verb and means that cannot be done
<thei>, know or be able, with <loin>, without, written as one word: without knowing, and after a verb without being able to do it
<theilo>, unable, with <liang>, even, written as one word after a verb: so much that one cannot even do it; with a clause before it, not even know
<theilo> cannot with <pa> marking a man; {pau theilopa} is the man who could not speak
<thei> know with <lo> not, <pi> and <a>: while not knowing

terms: those who do not know/the simple
definition: <theilo> not know with the plural <te>; {thu theilote} are the ignorant
<theilo.1> unable with the plural <te>, placed after a verb: the people who are not able to do what the verb says, as {laisim theilote}, those who cannot read
<thei>, able, and <lua>, very much, written as one word after a verb: it can very well happen or be done; after <hong> it can also be <thei>, know: know very well
<thei>, know or be able, and the emphatic <mah> written as one word: can certainly, may well; of knowing, know indeed
<thei> and <mahmah> written as one word: after a verb, be very able to or very apt to; alone, know very well
<thei>, can, and <mai>, simply, written as one word after a verb: it can simply be so, it may well happen
<thei> and <mawk> written as one word after a verb: can, may even, said of something surprising or not expected
<thei> fig with <moh> cake: figs pressed into a lump
plural of <theimoh>
the Burmese unit of one hundred thousand, used in counting money and people: {Thein 2} is 200,000; also a part of Burmese personal names
<thei>, able, with the noun suffix <na>, placed after a verb: being able to do it, or the place or way in which it can be done; {khawl theina ding} is so as to be able to stop
<thei>, fig or fruit tree, with {nah}, leaf: the leaf of the tree
<thei>, able, and <nai>, yet, written as one word and followed by <kei> or <lo>: not yet able to, cannot yet

terms: not yet know/not yet be able
definition: <thei> and <nailo> written as one word: not know yet; after another verb, not yet be able to, as in {gencian theinailo}, cannot yet say for certain
<thei> and <nawn> written as one word, followed by a negative such as <lo> or <kei>: can no longer, or no longer know

terms: can no longer/be no longer able
definition: <thei> and <nawnlo> written as one word after a verb: can no longer do it; standing alone, no longer know
<theinawnlo> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will not be able to do it any more
<thei>, know, with <ngei>, ever, written as one word: have known or experienced before; {ki theingei} is have known each other before
Zolai name of a month, {Theinosih kha}, which the book gives as February, the month of Zomi National Day
a month of the traditional Zomi calendar, set beside January in the book's table of month names
<thei>, fruit tree, and <nuai>, under, written as one word: the place under a fruit tree; listed by the book in the set pair {theinuai hainuai} without an explanation
<thei> know with <nuam> want
<theinuam> and <ta> written as one word; found in {a theinuamta ding in}, for those who want to know

terms: one who can/one who is able
definition: <thei> can, know how, with <pa> marking a man: the man who is able to, placed after a verb; with <aw> in address: {mi khem theipa aw}, you deceiver
<thei> know with <pa> marking a man: the man who knows; {lai theipa}, the man who knows writing, is the scribe or teacher of the Law
<thei> know with <pah> at once
<thei> can with <pah> at once, after a verb: {khua mukik theipah} is was able to see again immediately

terms: will be able at once/will know at once
definition: <theipah> and <ding> written as one word: will know a thing at once; after another verb, will be able to do it straight away

terms: be able right away/know at once
definition: <thei>, be able or know, with <pak>, quickly or for now, written as one word: can readily happen or be done, can be said for the moment, or notice in time

terms: not know at once/not be able right away
definition: <thei> and <paklo> written as one word: not know straight away, as in {acihnading theipaklo}, not know at once what to do; after another verb, not be able to do it readily
a fig that is ripe before the main season, from <thei> fig

terms: only then can/only then know/come to know
definition: <thei>, know or be able, with <pan>, here only then, written as one word: only at that point come to know, or become able to do what the verb before it says

terms: will only then be able/can only after that
definition: <thei>, <pan> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will be able to do it only then, not before the time or condition just named

terms: as much as possible/the most that can be
definition: <thei> able with the superlative ending {-pen}, most, written as one word after a describing word and usually followed by <in>: as much so as possible, as in {ahoih theipen in}, as well as possible
<thei>, be able, with <pha>, written as one word after a verb: well able to, quite likely to, or just manage to do it
<thei> know with <pih> together with: share the knowledge of a matter; {a theipih mite} are the witnesses
in {kisak theipih}, boast of something: be proud on account of it
<thei> and <pipi> written as one word: while knowing it, in spite of knowing; often followed by <mah> or <in>
fruit that a strong wind blows off the tree; in Luke 11:42 {anteh theipuam} stands for every kind of garden produce

fruit and garden produce of every kind, as the second half of the pairs {anteh theipuam}, vegetables and fruit, and {singgah theipuam}, fruit of all kinds; not only the unripe fruit of the first sense
the fruit of the fig tree
<thei> with <sa> marking a completed state; {a theisa mi}, those who knew someone before
<thei>, know, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to know, reveal
<theisak> make known with the linking suffix <in>
<thei> can with the causative <sak> and <kik> again, after a verb: {pau theisakkik} is make able to speak again, {khua mu theisakkik} make able to see again

terms: want to inform/wish to make known
definition: <theisak>, make known, and <nuam>, want, written as one word; {kong theisaknuam uhhi} is we wish to let you know
<thei>, able, with a softening second part, after a verb: be able to do it after all or to some degree; {theisam lo} is not really able either
<theisa> having known with the plural <te>: those who know someone

<thei>, can, and <zel>, repeatedly, written as one word after a verb: it can happen now and again, it tends to happen

small broken pieces or scraps of something; {vanleng themneng} is the wreckage of an aircraft
a very small amount or thing, placed after the noun: {thu themno khat}, a small matter
small broken bits, {a neng a themte} are the crumbs and broken pieces left over

<then> ten thousand doubled with the plural <te>, used with {tul-tul} thousands upon thousands
said of cloud and mist that pass away

expressive adverb said of spitting, as in {cilsia thepthup}; it seems to picture spitting again and again or here and there

of rain or dripping water: stop, let up; {a theu thei lo} is unceasing

placed after a verb: the action is done time after time or keeps happening
descriptive word placed after <kil>, said of long hair that is wavy or curly

<tho.2>, fly, with the marker <in.2> of the doer: the flies, as the ones that act

of a person's character, pleasant and easy to deal with, as in {mi thunuam}, a good-natured person, often with <mahmah>; a lasting quality, not kindness shown to one person with <tungah>
<thunuam> with the linking suffix <a>, describing the next noun; {thunuama biakna} is the fellowship or peace offering
{mi thunuamte} stands where the NIV has diligent hands, set against {a thadahte}, the lazy
what comes after a matter, from <thu> and <nung>; mostly in the pair <thunung thuma>, what follows a matter and what goes before it, all its ins and outs

<thunung>, what comes after a matter, and <thuma>, what comes before it: all that hangs on a matter, its consequences and further questions; {thunung thuma om loin} is without any more to it, without conditions
<thu>, matter, with <pai>, go: how a matter proceeds, mostly as {thupai zia} or {thupai dan}, the way things work; in some articles also a phrase or expression beside <laimal>, a word
<thu>, matter, and <paizia>, way of going, written as one word: how a matter proceeds, the proper order in which it is dealt with
<thu>, word or law, with <palsat>, transgress; {thupalsat mite} are transgressors
<thu>, word or law, with <palsat>, transgress, and the noun suffix <na>: the breaking of a law or command
<thupalsatna>, transgression, with the plural <te>
<thu>, word or law, with <palsat>, transgress, and the plural <te>: those who break the law
take part in a case at court; the verse has the Lord taking his place to do so
<thu>, matter, with <patna>, beginning: the opening part of an article, sermon or speech
<thu>, matter, and <pawlkhat>, some, written as one word: some matters, a number of things to say or to know
how God deals with the devious, {thukawi mi}; the base {thupeel} is not otherwise attested
<thu>, matter, with the topic marker <pen> written as one word: as for the matter, mostly as {hih thupen}, this matter
<thu>, word, with <pha>, good: a blessing; <thupha pia> is bless and {thupha ngah} is be blessed
<thupha>, blessing, written with a capital at the start of a sentence or as a title: {Thupha a ngah} is receive blessing or be blessed, and {Thupha a nei} is the Blessed One
<thupha>, blessing, and <hongpia>, give us or give you: bless; the closing wish of a letter or notice, with {Topa'n} before it and <hen> or <tahen> after it, may the Lord bless you
Saying: good news does not get past the door, bad news goes over nine ridges; good news spreads slowly, bad news spreads fast
<thupha>, blessing, and <naak>, spring or source: a person or thing from which blessing flows to others, as a spring gives water; said with <suak>, become, and of parents and of honouring them
<thupha>, blessing, and <pia>, give: bless; the one who blesses stands before it with <in> and the one blessed stands directly before it or with <tungah>

<thupha>, blessing, and <piakna>, giving: the benediction, the blessing that a minister speaks to close a service or a gathering; the name of the minister stands before it, and {tawpna thupha piakna} is the closing benediction
<thupha>, blessing, with <bawl>, do, written as one word: do good to someone, show kindness
<thu>, matter, with <phamawh>, serious, written as one word: a serious or urgent matter
<thupha> and <ngah> written as one word: having received blessing, blessed; {thuphangah minam} is a blessed people
<thupha> and <piakna> written as one word: the giving of a blessing, the benediction in a service
<thupha>, blessing, with the plural <te>; {Kha Siangtho piak thuphate} are the blessings the Holy Spirit gives, the spiritual gifts

<thu>, matter, with <phawk>, notice: be aware of how things stand and take them to heart; {thuphawk loin} is heedlessly or complacently, and {thuphawk theih lohna} is a heart that cannot take things in
<thuphawk>, take heed, with the noun suffix <na>: a warning that makes one aware; {thuphawkna ngah} is be warned
<thuphawk>, be aware of matters, with <sa>, already: experienced, having come to know how things are; said of men fit to lead
<thu>, matter, with <pi>, great: of great weight or worth; {a thupi lo} is unimportant, {thupi takin} is solemnly, and {thupi ngaihsut} is count as important

terms: I value/I appreciate/I hold in high regard
definition: <thupi>, important, and <kasa>, I find: I regard the person or thing named before it as important, said in thanks and tribute; often followed by <mahmah>

terms: be highly regarded/be admired/be thought important
definition: <thupi>, important or great, and <kisa>, be considered: be thought great, be held in high regard; the person or deed that is admired stands before it, often with <pen>, and <mahmah> often follows
<thu>, word, with <pia>, give: give an order or command; the form used before another word is <thupiak>
form of <thupia>, give an order, used before another word; {a thupiak bangin} is just as he commanded
used as a noun after the one who gives it: an order of a ruler, the police or God, as in {Pasian thupiak}, the command of God, and {Thupiak 10}, the Ten Commandments; sense 1 is the verb
<thupiak>, command, with <kholh>, beforehand, and the noun suffix <na>: a word given in advance about what is to come, a warning or revelation
<thupiak>, command, with the noun suffix <na>: a command or order; {thupiakna zui} or <mang> is keep a command
<thupiakna>, command, with the plural <te>
<thupiak>, command, with <sa>, already: what has been commanded; {a thupiaksa bangin} is just as he had commanded
<thupiaksa>, what has been commanded, with the plural <te>
<thupiak>, command, with the plural <te>
<thu>, matter, with <piang>, happen: what has happened or will happen; {thupiang khempeuh} is everything that happened

<thupiang>, a happening, and <ahihi>, it is: the closing formula of a news report, it is a thing that happened; the time or place with <in> or <ah> stands before it, and the report often opens with {hih thupiang pen}, this incident

terms: reportedly happened/is said to have happened
definition: <thupiang>, event, here used as a verb, the matter happened, with <kici>, it is said: closing formula of a news report, after the place with <ah> and the day with <in>, and followed by <hi>
<thupiang>, event, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: marks the incident as what the sentence is about; {hih thupiangpen} is as for this incident
<thupiang> with <sa>, here already, written as one word: something that has already happened, a past event or experience
<thupiang>, what happens, with <sa>, already, and the plural <te>: the things that have happened
<thupiang>, event, with the plural <te>: the things that happen or have happened
<thupiang>, event, with <teng>, all: everything that has happened, the whole matter
<thupi>, important, and <bawl>, make, written as one word: treat someone as important, give honour to
<thupi> and <ding> written as one word, mostly after a verb with <ding>: it is important to do so
a short saying that holds wisdom, <thu> with <pil>, wise; often paired with <paunak>
<thupi>, important, with <lak>, take: take seriously, treat as important; the same verse also writes it as {thupi takin lak}
<thupi>, important, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<thupi> and <lua> written as one word; with <lo> or <ahilo>, not so important
<thupi>, great or honorable, with the noun suffix <na>: dignity or splendor; {lungsim thupina} is integrity of heart
how much a thing matters, said of everyday things such as food, health or a habit and not of the splendor of a person; usually {a thupina}, its importance, after a verbal noun, or beside <manphatna>
<thupina>, greatness, with the plural <te>: the splendors or precious things someone once had, where the NIV has treasures
<thupi>, important, and <ngaihsut>, consider, written as one word: what a person or group counts as important; once glossed with English values
<thupi>, great, with <pen>, most: the greatest or most important
<thupi>, important, with <sa>, here feel or consider: regard a person or thing as important
<thupi>, important, with <sak>, hold to be: value highly, set great store by something
<thupisak> and <in> written as one word: holding something to be important, and so doing what follows
<thupisak>, value highly, with the noun suffix <na>: treating something as important, the high value set on it
<thupisak>, value highly, and <zaw>, more, written as one word; the thing compared stands before it with <sangin>
<thupi>, important, with <san>, take as: take seriously, not make light of; the NIV turns it round as do not despise
count as important, pay heed to; with <kei> or <lo> it means disregard or not listen to
<thupisim>, take seriously, and <lo>, not, written as one word
form of <thupi>, important, used before words such as <lam>, <sak>, <ngaihsut> and <luatna>; {a thupit lam} is how important it is

<thupit>, important, and <ngaihsut>, think: to hold a thing or person to be important; the thing valued stands before the pair and the subject marker comes between them and it, as in {i thupit ngaihsut}
<thupi>, great or important, and <tak> written as one word: in a great, grand or solemn way, mostly as {thupitak in}; before a noun, great
<thupitak> with <in>, written as one word: in a grand, solemn or important way
plural of <thupi>, said of persons or things of high rank or importance; {mi thupite} is the great, the mighty
<thupi> important with <teng> all of: the things that matter most, the valuable things
<thupit>, the form of <thupi>, be great, be important, used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: impressive
<thupi>, great, with the noun suffix <na>: majesty, greatness
<thupi>, important, with the noun suffix <na>: how much a person, thing or matter counts, as in {hun thupitna}, the importance of time; not the majesty of God or a king
<thupitna>, greatness, with the plural <te>: the splendors or precious things someone once had, where the NIV has treasures
form of <thupisak> used before <ding> and when the verb stands as a noun: {ih thupitsak} is what we hold important
<thupit>, the form of <thupi>, be great, be important, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: magnify; the page lists the form without a meaning

terms: deserving honour/fit to be counted great
definition: <thupit>, the form of <thupi>, be great, be important, used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: deserving honour
<thupit> with <zia>, manner, written as one word: how important or great someone or something is
<thupi>, great or important, with the comparative <zaw>: greater, worth more; the thing compared is marked by <sangin>, than
<thu>, matter, and <poimawh>, important, written as one word
<thu> with <pom>, hold fast: what a person or a church holds to be true, a doctrine or conviction
the way a matter is held, from <thu>, <pom>, hold fast, and <zia>, manner: what a person or a church believes about something
<thupomzia>, belief or view, with the plural <te>: the beliefs or views a person holds
<thu>, word, with <puak>, carry or send: a message or news brought to someone, also an order sent; {thupuak pa} is a messenger
<thupuak>, message, with the noun ending {-na}: the sending of a message, or the message or statement sent out
<thupuak>, word that is carried, with the plural <te>: those who bring the message
<thu>, word, with <pulak>, make known: announce something to a gathering or to the public; in a programme also the heading for the one who makes the announcements; <thupulakna> is the announcement
<thu>, word, with <pulakna>, announcement: a public statement by an organisation or office; <thupulakna nei> is issue a statement

<thupulakna>, a statement, and <nei>, hold: the regular verb for a body or a spokesman that makes a public statement; the issuer stands before it with <in> or <pan>, and what was said comes before it closed by <ci-in>
